Here is the report:

### Q1
`STORE_MODE` is read in `Store.__init__` at `src/inventory/store.py:41`; the three accepted values map to permission tables handed to the backend (line 58). For `open`, no table is passed and every operation is allowed (line 44). For `append-only`, writes to `items` and `logs` are allowed but deletes are refused (lines 46-51). For `read-only`, only listing and reading are allowed, with the lock directory as the one writable exception (lines 52-55). Any other value raises a `ConfigError` naming the accepted values (line 57).
Evidence: `src/inventory/store.py:41`
Evidence: `src/inventory/store.py:44`
Evidence: `src/inventory/store.py:46-51`
Evidence: `src/inventory/store.py:52-55`
Evidence: `src/inventory/store.py:57-58`

### Q2
`Store.open` (`src/inventory/store.py:90-121`) first opens the backend (line 92); a missing backend raises `NotFound` before anything needs closing. It then loads `meta/marker` and compares it with the expected constant (lines 96-99), loads `meta/version` and checks it against the supported set (lines 100-104), and loads `meta/id`, decoding it to 16 bytes (line 106). Only an unsupported version closes the backend before raising. The lock is taken last, at line 118, and only when the caller asked for one.
Evidence: `src/inventory/store.py:90-121`
Evidence: `src/inventory/store.py:96-99`
Evidence: `src/inventory/store.py:100-104`
Evidence: `src/inventory/store.py:118`

### Q3
Each stored record is framed by `pack_record` in `src/inventory/framing.py:22-48`: a fixed 12-byte header carrying the payload length and a CRC32 of the header itself, followed by the compressed payload. The reader in `unpack_record` (lines 51-80) verifies the header checksum first and rejects a length that would run past the buffer (lines 60-63) before decompressing. The payload has no checksum of its own; integrity of the content rests on the keyed digest described in Q4.
Evidence: `src/inventory/framing.py:22-48`
Evidence: `src/inventory/framing.py:51-80`
Evidence: `src/inventory/framing.py:60-63`

### Q4
Record identity is a keyed digest computed in `Keys.record_id` (`src/inventory/keys.py:31-38`) over the uncompressed payload, so two equal payloads share one id. Authentication of stored content therefore comes from recomputing that digest after decompression (`src/inventory/store.py:140-146`); neither the cached digests nor the signed headers serve this role. Tampering that preserves the header checksum is caught at that recomputation, not earlier.
Evidence: `src/inventory/keys.py:31-38`
Evidence: `src/inventory/store.py:140-146`
Evidence: `src/inventory/keys.py:40-44`
